question: Who among the following is known for his/her books 'The Algebra of Infinite Justice', 'Kashmir: The Case for Freedom' and 'Capitalism: A Ghost Story'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arundhati Roy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Algebra of Infinite Justice", "Kashmir: The Case for Freedom" and "Capitalism: A Ghost Story" were written by Arundhati Roy, a well-known Indian author and activist. (अरुंधति रॉय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize (1997) for her debut novel "The God of Small Things". Her second novel is "The Ministry of Utmost Happiness".

• She is also known for her non-fiction essays on politics, environment and social justice.

NOTE

• Author–work pairs: Midnight's Children (Salman Rushdie), The Shadow Lines / The Hungry Tide (Amitav Ghosh), Interpreter of Maladies (Jhumpa Lahiri).

question: Few renowned artists of __________ dance style in India are Roshan Kumari, Shovana Narayan, Maya Rao and Kumudini Lakhia.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Roshan Kumari, Shovana Narayan, Maya Rao and Kumudini Lakhia are all renowned exponents of the Kathak classical dance form of North India. (कथक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kathak is known for its fast footwork (tatkar), spins (chakkars) and expressive storytelling (abhinaya).

• Its major gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms: Kathak (North India), Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: Moti Masjid in Agra fort was constructed by which of the following Mughal Emperors?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shahjahan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Moti Masjid" (Pearl Mosque) in the Agra Fort was constructed by the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan. Built of white marble, it is famous for its pristine, pearl-like beauty. (मोती मस्जिद, आगरा — शाहजहाँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Shah Jahan is regarded as the greatest builder among the Mughals; his reign is called the "Golden Age of Mughal Architecture".

• His famous monuments include the Taj Mahal (Agra), the Red Fort and Jama Masjid (Delhi).

• There is another famous Moti Masjid inside the Red Fort, Delhi, built by Aurangzeb.

NOTE

• The Agra Fort (a UNESCO World Heritage Site) was originally built by Akbar; Shah Jahan added several white-marble structures to it.

question: To get relief from constipation, which of the following is prescribed to be eaten in large amount?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fibre.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To get relief from constipation, a diet rich in "fibre (roughage)" is prescribed. Fibre adds bulk to the stool and helps in easy and regular bowel movements. (रेशा / फाइबर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Good sources of dietary fibre: whole grains, fruits, vegetables, pulses and salads.

• Fibre itself is not digested/absorbed by the body but is essential for a healthy digestive system.

NOTE

• Nutrients: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water and roughage (fibre). Drinking plenty of water along with fibre helps prevent constipation.

question: Who among the following was the top run-scorer for India at the 1983 Cricket World Cup final with 38 runs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Krishnamachari Srikkanth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the 1983 Cricket World Cup final (India vs West Indies at Lord's), Krishnamachari Srikkanth was India's top run-scorer with 38 runs. India famously won its first World Cup in that match. (के. श्रीकांत — 38 रन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India, captained by Kapil Dev, defeated the West Indies to win the 1983 World Cup.

• Mohinder Amarnath was the Man of the Match in the final (for his all-round performance with bat and ball).

NOTE

• India won the ODI World Cup in 1983 and 2011, and the T20 World Cup in 2007 and 2024. Kapil Dev's unbeaten 175 against Zimbabwe in the 1983 tournament is legendary.

question: Where was the Intercontinental Football Cup 2023 organised?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhubaneswar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Intercontinental Football Cup 2023 was organised in Bhubaneswar, Odisha (at the Kalinga Stadium). India won the title, beating Lebanon in the final. (इंटरकांटिनेंटल कप 2023 — भुवनेश्वर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Intercontinental Cup is an international football tournament organised by the All India Football Federation (AIFF).

• It was the 3rd edition of the tournament; India had also won the inaugural 2018 edition.

NOTE

• Sunil Chhetri is India's football captain and one of the highest international goal-scorers. Odisha has become a major hub for hosting sports events (hockey, football).

question: In 1974, classical singer Naina Devi was awarded the Padma Shri for her contribution to which of the following singing styles?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thumri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The classical singer Naina Devi was awarded the Padma Shri in 1974 for her contribution to "Thumri", a semi-classical vocal form of Hindustani music. (नैना देवी — ठुमरी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Thumri is a romantic/devotional semi-classical genre, often based on themes of love (Radha–Krishna). It allows greater expressive freedom than pure classical khayal.

• Naina Devi was also a prominent broadcaster and promoter of Hindustani music.

NOTE

• Semi-classical Hindustani vocal forms: Thumri, Dadra, Tappa, Kajari, Chaiti and Ghazal. Famous thumri singers include Begum Akhtar, Girija Devi and Shobha Gurtu.

question: What is the chemical formula for the compound commonly known as 'laughing gas'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is N₂O.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Laughing gas" is the common name for "nitrous oxide", whose chemical formula is "N₂O". It is used as a mild anaesthetic (in dentistry/surgery) and produces a feeling of euphoria (hence "laughing gas"). (हास्य गैस — नाइट्रस ऑक्साइड, N₂O)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• N₂O was discovered by Joseph Priestley and its anaesthetic properties were noted by Humphry Davy.

• Other oxides of nitrogen: NO (nitric oxide), NO₂ (nitrogen dioxide), N₂O₃, N₂O₅.

NOTE

• Common name–formula pairs for SSC: Laughing gas – N₂O, Marsh gas – CH₄, Baking soda – NaHCO₃, Washing soda – Na₂CO₃, Quick lime – CaO.

question: In which of the following religions was the agriculture prohibited for its followers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jainism.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Jainism, agriculture was (traditionally) prohibited/discouraged for its followers because ploughing the land could kill insects, worms and other small living beings, which violates the core principle of "Ahimsa (non-violence)". (जैन धर्म — कृषि निषेध)

• This is one reason many Jains traditionally took up trade and commerce instead.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ahimsa (non-violence) is the supreme principle of Jainism; Jains take great care to avoid harming any living being.

• The five vows of Jainism: Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Aparigraha and Brahmacharya.

NOTE

• Jainism was propagated by Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara. Its two main sects are Digambara and Svetambara.

question: According to National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023 (A Progress Review), which state has the highest proportion of multidimensionally poor people (Headcount Ratio)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2023: A Progress Review by NITI Aayog, Bihar had the highest proportion of multidimensionally poor people (Headcount Ratio) among the states. (बिहार — सर्वाधिक बहुआयामी गरीबी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• After Bihar, the states with high multidimensional poverty were Jharkhand and Meghalaya.

• The MPI measures poverty across three dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living — through 12 indicators, based on the OPHI–UNDP methodology.

NOTE

• A person is "multidimensionally poor" if deprived in at least one-third (weighted) of the indicators. The report noted a large fall in poverty between 2015-16 and 2019-21.

question: Who was the Viceroy of India when the Indian Arms Act, 1878, was passed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Lytton.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian Arms Act, 1878, was passed during the viceroyalty of Lord Lytton. This Act prohibited Indians from keeping arms without a licence, while exempting Europeans — a clearly discriminatory law. (भारतीय शस्त्र अधिनियम, 1878 — लॉर्ड लिटन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Lord Lytton (Viceroy 1876–1880) also passed the repressive Vernacular Press Act, 1878 (to curb the Indian-language press) and held the grand Delhi Durbar (1877), proclaiming Queen Victoria as "Kaiser-i-Hind".

• His policies during a severe famine (the "Great Famine of 1876–78") were widely criticised.

NOTE

• The Vernacular Press Act was later repealed by Lord Ripon, known for the Ripon's Resolution on Local Self-Government (1882) — he is called the "Father of Local Self-Government in India".

question: According to Economic Survey 2023-24, which of the following states is the largest wheat producing state of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Economic Survey 2023-24, Uttar Pradesh is the largest wheat-producing state of India. (उत्तर प्रदेश — सर्वाधिक गेहूँ उत्पादक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Uttar Pradesh is followed by Madhya Pradesh and Punjab in wheat production.

• Wheat is the main Rabi (winter) crop of India; it needs a cool growing season and a bright sunny harvest time.

• India is the second-largest producer of wheat in the world (after China).

NOTE

• The Green Revolution (1960s, led by M. S. Swaminathan) greatly boosted wheat production, especially in Punjab, Haryana and western UP.

question: Which Article deals with the provisions in case of failure of the constitutional machinery in the State?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 356.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 356 of the Constitution deals with the provisions in case of failure of the constitutional machinery in a State, commonly known as "President's Rule" or "State Emergency". (अनुच्छेद 356 — राष्ट्रपति शासन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Under President's Rule, the State government is dismissed, the State Legislative Assembly is either suspended or dissolved, and the state is governed directly by the Centre (through the Governor on behalf of the President).

• It is initially imposed for 6 months and can be extended up to a maximum of 3 years (with conditions).

NOTE

• The three types of emergencies: National Emergency (Article 352), President's Rule / State Emergency (Article 356) and Financial Emergency (Article 360). The S. R. Bommai case (1994) laid down guidelines on the use of Article 356.

question: The Indian Constitution has adopted the parliamentary form of Government from __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Britain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian Constitution adopted the parliamentary form of government (the "Westminster model") from Britain (the United Kingdom). (संसदीय शासन प्रणाली — ब्रिटेन से)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other features borrowed from Britain: the Rule of Law, single citizenship, the law-making procedure, the office of the Speaker, and the idea of a nominal head (the President).

• Key features of the parliamentary system: a nominal executive (President) and a real executive (PM & Council of Ministers), collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha, and majority-party rule.

NOTE

• Borrowed features: Fundamental Rights, Judicial Review (USA); DPSP (Ireland); Concurrent List (Australia); Emergency provisions (Germany); Fundamental Duties (erstwhile USSR).

question: According to average rainfall in India, the Ladakh Union Territory is located in __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is areas of inadequate rainfall.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ladakh receives very little rainfall — it is located in an area of inadequate (scanty/very low) rainfall (generally less than 50 cm per year). It is a cold desert, lying in the rain shadow of the Himalayas. (लद्दाख — अपर्याप्त वर्षा वाला क्षेत्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ladakh lies beyond the reach of the monsoon (blocked by the Himalayas), so it is extremely dry and cold, resembling a cold desert like the Tibetan plateau.

• India's rainfall is classified as areas of high (>200 cm), medium (100–200 cm), low (50–100 cm) and inadequate/scanty (<50 cm) rainfall.

NOTE

• Other scanty-rainfall regions: western Rajasthan (Thar Desert), parts of Gujarat, the leeward side of the Western Ghats, and Ladakh.

question: Due to the popularity of Indian clothes in Britain, a law was passed to ban Indian clothes. Which of the following was that law?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calico Act.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Due to the great popularity of Indian cotton textiles (especially calico and muslin) in Britain, the British Parliament passed the "Calico Act" (early 18th century) to ban/restrict the import and use of Indian printed cotton cloth, in order to protect the British textile industry. (कैलिको अधिनियम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Calico" is a type of plain cotton cloth that originally came from Calicut (Kozhikode), Kerala — hence the name.

• Such protectionist laws hurt the Indian handloom/textile industry and are examples of the economic exploitation of India.

NOTE

• Indian textiles like muslin (Dhaka), calico and chintz were world-famous. British policies and the Industrial Revolution led to the decline (de-industrialisation) of India's traditional textile industry.

question: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder in teenagers. Here body weight:
solution_text:
The correct answer is loses drastically.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Anorexia nervosa" is an eating disorder in which a person (often a teenager) eats very little due to an intense fear of gaining weight, causing the body weight to drop/reduce drastically. (एनोरेक्सिया नर्वोसा — वजन में भारी कमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• People with anorexia have a distorted body image and severely restrict their food intake, which can lead to serious health problems.

• It is different from "bulimia nervosa", another eating disorder involving binge-eating followed by purging.

NOTE

• This is a sensitive health topic; the focus here is purely the factual effect on body weight tested in exams. Such disorders require professional medical and psychological care.

question: Carbon dioxide plays a vital role in changing the earth's climate, leading to a critical condition known as __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Greenhouse Effect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is a major greenhouse gas. It traps heat radiated from the Earth's surface, warming the atmosphere — this is called the "Greenhouse Effect", which leads to global warming and climate change. (ग्रीनहाउस प्रभाव)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Major greenhouse gases: Carbon dioxide (CO₂), Methane (CH₄), Nitrous oxide (N₂O), Water vapour and CFCs.

• Excess greenhouse gases (from burning fossil fuels, deforestation, etc.) intensify the effect, causing global warming, melting glaciers and rising sea levels.

NOTE

• "Ozone depletion" (a different problem) is caused mainly by CFCs damaging the ozone layer. International efforts: the Kyoto Protocol and the Paris Agreement aim to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

question: 'Navroz' is celebrated as the new year by which of the following communities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parsi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Navroz" (also spelt Nowruz) is celebrated as the New Year by the Parsi (Zoroastrian) community. It marks the beginning of the Persian/Zoroastrian calendar. (नवरोज़ — पारसी समुदाय का नववर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Navroz" literally means "new day". In India, the Parsi community (originally from Persia/Iran) celebrates it with prayers, feasts and community gatherings.

• The Parsis follow Zoroastrianism, one of the world's oldest religions, founded by the prophet Zarathustra (Zoroaster).

NOTE

• Festivals by community: Eid (Muslim), Christmas/Easter (Christian), Buddha Purnima (Buddhist), Baisakhi/Guru Nanak Jayanti (Sikh), Navroz (Parsi), Paryushana (Jain).

question: Odissi Guru, __________, received the first Utkal Pratibha Samman 2023 at Bhubaneswar.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ratikant Mohapatra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Odissi Guru Ratikant Mohapatra received the first Utkal Pratibha Samman 2023 at Bhubaneswar for his contribution to the classical dance form Odissi. (रतिकांत महापात्र — ओडिसी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ratikant Mohapatra is the son and disciple of the legendary Odissi maestro Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, and he heads the Srjan (Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Odissi Nrityabasa) institution.

• Odissi is the classical dance of Odisha, known for the graceful tribhanga posture and themes from the Gita Govinda.

NOTE

• Odisha (capital Bhubaneswar, the "Temple City") is the home of Odissi dance, the Jagannath Temple (Puri) and the Sun Temple (Konark).

question: Which of the followings is NOT one of the government accounts of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is General Provident Fund.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The three government accounts (funds) of India are the Consolidated Fund of India, the Public Account of India, and the Contingency Fund of India. The "General Provident Fund" is NOT one of these three funds. (सामान्य भविष्य निधि — तीन सरकारी निधियों में से नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Consolidated Fund of India (Article 266) — all revenues, loans and receipts of the government; withdrawals need parliamentary approval.

• Public Account of India (Article 266) — money held by the government in trust (e.g., provident funds, small savings); does not need parliamentary approval for payments.

• Contingency Fund of India (Article 267) — for meeting unforeseen/urgent expenditure; at the disposal of the President.

NOTE

• The General Provident Fund (GPF) is actually a savings scheme for government employees, and the money in it forms part of the Public Account.

question: To mark the 75 years of Indo-Lanka Diplomatic Relations, External Affairs Minister Jaishankar inaugurated the 'Geoffrey Bawa: It is Essential To be There' Exhibition in March 2023. Who was Geoffrey Bawa?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sri Lankan Architect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Geoffrey Bawa was a famous Sri Lankan architect, considered one of the most influential Asian architects of the 20th century and a pioneer of "tropical modernism". (जेफ्री बावा — श्रीलंकाई वास्तुकार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The exhibition "Geoffrey Bawa: It is Essential to be There" was inaugurated by External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar in March 2023 to mark 75 years of India–Sri Lanka diplomatic relations.

• Geoffrey Bawa's works blend modern architecture with local traditions and the natural landscape.

NOTE

• India and Sri Lanka share deep historical, cultural and religious ties (e.g., Buddhism, the Ramayana connection). India follows a "Neighbourhood First" policy.

question:
Based on the Tendulkar committee, the National poverty line was defined as which of the following?

i. ₹816 per capita per month for rural areas   ii. ₹1,000 per capita per month for urban areas.
option_2: Both i and ii are correct
option_3: Both i and ii are incorrect
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both i and ii are correct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Based on the Tendulkar Committee, the national poverty line was defined as ₹816 per capita per month for rural areas and ₹1,000 per capita per month for urban areas (for 2011-12). So both statements i and ii are correct. (तेंदुलकर समिति — गरीबी रेखा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Tendulkar Committee (2009), headed by Suresh Tendulkar, revised the methodology for estimating poverty, moving beyond just calorie intake to include spending on health and education.

• The Rangarajan Committee (2014) later suggested higher poverty-line figures.

NOTE

• Poverty estimation in India was traditionally done by the Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog) using data from the National Sample Survey (NSS).

question: Amer Fort was built with red sandstone and white marble by which ruler in the 16th century?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raja Man Singh I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Amer (Amber) Fort near Jaipur, Rajasthan, built with red sandstone and white marble, was constructed by Raja Man Singh I in the 16th century. (आमेर किला — राजा मानसिंह प्रथम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Raja Man Singh I was a trusted general (one of the Navaratnas) in the court of the Mughal Emperor Akbar.

• The Amer Fort is famous for its Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace), Diwan-i-Aam and Diwan-i-Khas, and is part of the "Hill Forts of Rajasthan", a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• Later, Sawai Jai Singh II founded the city of Jaipur (1727) and shifted the capital from Amer to Jaipur. He also built the Jantar Mantar observatories.

question: In 2023, Congress MP Shashi Tharoor has been named as the chairperson of the Parliamentary Committee on __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chemicals and Fertilisers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2023, Congress MP Dr. Shashi Tharoor was named the Chairperson of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Chemicals and Fertilisers. (शशि थरूर — रसायन एवं उर्वरक संबंधी समिति)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Parliamentary Standing Committees examine bills, budgets and the working of ministries in detail and aid Parliament's oversight function.

• Dr. Shashi Tharoor, an MP from Thiruvananthapuram, had earlier chaired the Standing Committee on External Affairs and the Committee on Information Technology.

NOTE

• The Department-Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) were introduced in 1993 for the detailed scrutiny of the demands for grants and bills of various ministries.
